idiom_name: nested key class whose constructor parameter type is the authorised class's private static brand (compile-time gate plus runtime check)
implementation_notes: TypeScript's private is checked only by the compiler and erased at run time, but it is enough to build a class-granular gate: give the authorised class a private static brand and let the nested key class take a parameter of type typeof Brand, a unique symbol. No code outside the class body can name the brand, so the key constructor is uncallable there - the compiler rejects the forged call with 'Argument of type symbol is not assignable to parameter of type unique symbol' - while the authorised class constructs keys normally. Because the brand is erased, keep the runtime comparison inside the key constructor whenever the compiled JavaScript also has to hold, or use # fields, which MDN documents as enforced by the engine after compilation. When the grantee is the module, the simpler realisation is a module-scoped key class with a private constructor that is never exported.
pitfalls: A private constructor on the key class blocks the authorised class too ('Constructor is private and only accessible within the class declaration'); nest the key and gate construction with a brand parameter instead.
private and typeof Brand vanish at run time, so without the runtime comparison the compiled JavaScript accepts any symbol.
InstanceType<typeof Factory.Key> is accurate but awkward; hiding it behind a module alias tends to widen the surface that consumers can name.
